02 · Your first workflow

Set up your first workflow

Pick one task that eats into your week and make it run the same way every time.

  1. Pick one task

    Choose something that repeats, like answering inquiries, confirming bookings, or sending a weekly report.

  2. Write down the steps

    List who does it, which tools they use, and what “done” looks like. That list is your first SOP.

  3. Automate or hand off one step

    Use a form, a template, or an automation for one step, or hand it to a team member or VA with the SOP. Review it after two weeks.

Want help setting this up? Request a discovery call ↗

03 · Trends to watch

Trends to watch

AI that works across formats

Turn one source brief into several useful deliverables.Open

How to use it

Create a source brief with product facts, dates, claims, tone, and the audience. Use it for each format so the details remain consistent.

Try it

Write one brief for your next offer, then use it for the caption, the flyer, and the email so every detail matches.

Before you rely on it

Check every version against the same brief before it goes out.

AI connected to business tools

Understand how an assistant can use information from other apps.Open

How to use it

Begin with a read-only task, like drafting a weekly summary from your sales sheet. Define what information the assistant can access and what it is allowed to change.

Try it

Have an assistant read your new leads each morning and draft follow-up messages for you to approve.

Before you rely on it

Check that the workflow exposes only fields needed for the task and that changes have a clear owner.

Review steps in automation

Build approval into actions that affect clients or records.Open

How to use it

Separate drafting from execution. Write down who approves an action, what they need to check, and where failures are recorded.

Try it

Before an automation emails customers, have it send drafts to you or a team member to approve first.

Before you rely on it

Verify there is a clear audit trail and a reliable way to resume a failed step.

Research and content

Brief an assistant, research topics, and write content.

Guide

Prompting and briefing

Build a brief an assistant can follow.Open

How to use it

Write down the task, audience, source material, and what a finished deliverable looks like. Include one example of the tone you want and tell the assistant to flag missing details.

Practice project

Give it a fictional café FAQ and ask for replies to questions about reservations, dietary options, and private events.

Before you deliver

Check every answer against the FAQ. Flag policies that require an owner’s decision.

How to use it

Practice project

Before you deliver

Guide

Content research

Find audience questions and turn verified answers into a content brief.Open

Start with the audience

Define who you want to reach and what decision they’re trying to make. Collect recurring questions from client FAQs, search suggestions, and customer reviews. Record the source and date for each question.

Check the evidence

Review existing coverage and note what it leaves unanswered. Verify facts with primary sources, and confirm business-specific details with the client. Flag claims that still need a source.

Build a brief

Pick one question and write the intended audience, search intent, angle, outline, sources, and next action. Adapt the brief for a blog, an FAQ, or social posts.

Practice project

Research what customers ask before booking a home service, like cleaning or moving. Group five questions by intent, pick one worth answering, and write a brief with two verified sources.

GitHub skills

  • Content Research Writer · Develop an outline and track sources while researching and drafting.
  • SEO Fundamentals · Match topics to search intent and identify relevant keywords.
  • Content Creator · Turn research findings into channel-specific ideas and a content calendar.

Sales and follow-up

Prepare useful sales conversations and track next steps.Open

How to use it

Capture the customer’s needs, buying timeline, and decision criteria. Use that context to draft a recap and prepare answers to common objections.

SEO research and reporting

Identify search opportunities and turn findings into prioritized work.Open

How to use it

Match each page to a customer’s intent. Inspect titles, page content, internal links, and indexability. Validate search data before quoting volumes or results.

Before you deliver

Record the baseline and what changed. Use Search Console data to evaluate performance when available.

Email and SMS campaigns

Plan useful messages around offers and customer timing.Open

How to use it

Start with the audience segment, offer, and single next step. Draft a short sequence with a send schedule and clarify who approves the copy.

Practice project

Draft a catering announcement email and one reminder SMS. Check links, deadlines, and unsubscribe behavior in a test send.

Before you deliver

Track attributed sales, clicks, and unsubscribes in the reporting window. Check consent and channel rules before sending.

Website animation and 3D

Use motion to explain layout changes and guide attention.Open

How to use it

Start with a useful interaction such as an expandable case study or a gallery. Keep motion short and make controls available by keyboard. Reserve 3D for a visual that benefits from depth.

Practice project

Prototype a portfolio image viewer with a subtle open transition and a reduced-motion version.

Before you deliver

Check that the interaction works without animation and that it stays responsive on mobile.

For freelancers and VAs · Video and animation

Video and animation workflow

Open each connected step to see which skills to use and how to apply them.

Video & Animation
Plan

Choose a format, write a three-beat storyboard, and list the footage, text, and audio each beat needs.

hyperframes:hyperframes ↗ · Plan an HTML-based video
Describe the audience, runtime, aspect ratio, and scene order. Ask for a timed outline first.
Edit

Time the visuals against the story before adding motion.

hyperframes:hyperframes-cli ↗ · Preview and render HTML video
Open the composition in preview, scrub each cut, and render once the timing works.
remotion-best-practices ↗ · Edit video in React
Set the composition duration and frame rate, then place each shot and caption on its frame range.
imagegen ↗ · Create supporting visuals
Ask for artwork or backgrounds in the final aspect ratio and place the selected asset in the edit.
Animate

Choose motion tools based on where the finished work will play.

animate ↗ · Design purposeful motion
Describe what changes and when. Ask for a short transition and a reduced-motion treatment.
Motion AI Kit ↗ · Refine interface transitions
Give the assistant the component and its start and end states. Ask it to check Motion’s guidance on easing or springs.
gsap-plugins ↗ · Animate layouts, SVG, or text
Choose the plugin that fits the effect, register it once, and test the interaction with reduced motion.
three-js ↗ · Build spatial motion
Describe the scene, camera, and lighting. Prototype one movement and check how it performs on mobile.
scroll-experience ↗ · Connect movement to scrolling
Define where the effect starts and ends, then check that the content stays readable without motion.
Review

Check timing, readability, and accessibility before sharing.

hyperframes:hyperframes-cli ↗ · Review the rendered video
Inspect the opening, scene changes, and final frame. Check captions and audio in the exported file.
agent-browser ↗ · Test web animation in a browser
Open the page, trigger the animation with mouse and keyboard, and check the mobile layout and reduced-motion behavior.
